speech:
Alright, Grizzly Rips, pull up a chair. Tuesday was a C, and I'm not going to dress it up. 1 win, 2 draws, 2 losses. We scored 10 and gave up 15. That's 3 goals conceded every single match, and you can't build a house when the back door's hanging off its hinges. Usually we pick up about 1.47 points a match and come out roughly even on goals. Today we got 1 point a match and finished minus 5. That's below our own standard, plain and simple.

The low point was Gurjots Army. 4-0. We didn't lose that one, we got folded up like a lawn chair. We also started cold all day: 1 point from the first halves, 4 from the second. Y'all kept waking up after the alarm had already gone off.

On the ladder, we started the day in Division 3 with 0 of 12 points and 3 chances left. We finished still in Division 3 with 5 of 12 and 1 chance left. That's 7 points short of promotion, and that clock is ticking.

BellyTb1, I'll be honest, you were the best thing on the pitch. 7 goals, 2 Man of the Match awards, a hat-trick against Boko harma, and a 9.4 in that wild 4-4. You averaged 8.4 when your usual is 7.33. You played like somebody who'd had enough of losing. But against Gurjots you went 0% on target when you usually hit 81%, and that's when we needed you most. You won 5 tackles out of 13, and you missed 3 against Boko. Belly, a striker who tracks back is worth two who don't.

PhogsToffees, you were the engine and the leaky radiator, all in one afternoon. 6 assists and 13 key passes means you were seeing the field like a hawk over a cornfield, and that 9.7 to finish the night was special. But 1 tackle won out of 19 is 5%, and your usual is 34%. Against FFC Bradar you gave the ball away 14 times and missed 6 tackles. Then against Boko you hit 33% of your shots when you usually hit 68%. Your 7.0 against Gurjots was you drifting out of a match we needed you in. Your passing carried us. Your defending let us down.

Now, finishing. We're hitting the target, so let's start picking corners. Keepers love a shot down the middle like I love a free refill. From an angle, finesse it to the far post. One-on-one, go low and hard. Only use timed finishing when you trust it, because a clean shot in the corner beats a rocket that sails into the parking lot. And low across the keeper is the hardest save there is, plus it sets up an easy rebound tap-in.

Here's the thing, friends. On average we outplayed every team we faced today. Our 8.21 rating beat their 7.86. We finished the day stronger than we started it. That 4-4 was a team that refused to quit. Tighten up the back, pick those corners, and come out swinging from the first whistle. I believe in y'all, and tomorrow we find out what we're made of.
